# Replace old FM ADR paths with explicit canonical redirects

## Context and problem
After Institution publishes the five FM ADRs, old Engine URLs and repository references must continue guiding readers without ingesting a second authoritative decision. Deleting the paths breaks existing citations; retaining full copies creates competing writers.

## Architectural reality
Engine owns the five old numbered ADR files and its README/VISION, architecture/discovery guides and tree inputs. Brain's admitted catalog and redirect-aware graph/KB/census readers provide authority; Engine's publication companion declares the public site outcome.

## The fix
Replace only the five old FM records with the accepted explicit redirect document shape, without ADR-authority frontmatter. Reconcile the complete Engine reference census, including bare-number references, to canonical custody while preserving historical origins. Use the accepted publication path and generated-input pipeline. Bind the exact Institution source revision and migration manifest used for the cut.

## Contract Ledger
| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback / edge case | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Old 0020/0032/0034/0037/0038 paths | D19427 §5 + amended 0006 | Human-readable canonical pointers classified as redirects, not ADRs | Unavailable destination remains explicit; no stale copy claims authority | Five pointers | Actual graph, both KB paths and seam reader classify them correctly |
| Engine discovery and old URLs | D19427 §§3,5,7 | Same decision remains findable from existing links | Ambiguous old reference names candidates; no current-custodian guess | Affected source references/tree inputs | Full reference census and rendered old→canonical journeys |
| Cross-repo cut binding | D19427 §§2,6 | Source hashes and manifest preconditions identify one authority | Drift/interruption refuses or preserves last admitted state; validated recovery route | Cut receipt | Candidate and post-merge live graph/KB/site readback |

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: The five old paths contain only the declared redirect shape; all readers classify them as non-ADR pointers.
- [ ] AC2: A complete reference sweep, including qualified and bare-number citations, leaves no broken load-bearing Engine reference or fabricated historical origin.
- [ ] AC3: Built-candidate old and canonical URLs reach the declared semantic destination; unavailable and interrupted move states stay explicit.
- [ ] AC4: The cut names the exact Institution revision and reviewed manifest, confirms reader/guidance adoption, and retains a tested recovery route.
- [ ] AC5: The candidate cut packet proves the reader controls and records parent-owned post-merge checks for one canonical indexed document, typed graph identity, preserved edges/shared vectors, old/qualified citation resolution and deployed reader behavior. The parent stays open until the live witnesses exist.

## Out of scope and avoided traps
No duplicate full ADR copy, unrelated retirement or blanket source move. Generated outputs remain pipeline-owned. No silent site downgrade or release-gate expansion.
Decision Record impact: aligned-with accepted 0006/0031/0040; no new semantics for the moved records.

unowned-rationale: planned dependency-bound delivery; a peer self-selects when the native prerequisites clear. Sophie retains coordination on the parent.
